facts.text: Rancho Santa Fe began as a Mexican land grant called Rancho San Dieguito in 1841, later renamed in 1921 by the Santa Fe Land Improvement Company.
The community was planned by the Santa Fe Land Improvement Company after a failed eucalyptus timber experiment, leading to a model rural residential area for “gentleman farmers.”.
In 1906 the Atchison, Topeka & Santa Fe Railway planted blue‑gum eucalyptus trees on the grant to produce railroad ties, but the wood proved too soft for spikes.
Rancho Santa Fe’s Village, designed by Requa and Jackson with architect Lilian Rice, showcases Spanish Colonial Revival style still visible in the Inn and row houses.
The town was designated a California Historical Landmark in 1989, with a 2004 amendment recognizing its unique cultural landscape.
Famous NFL quarterback Drew Brees lived in Rancho Santa Fe from 2003 to 2012, making the town a brief home for a sports legend.
